entities.name: Eric of Brandenburg
entities.label: Person
entities.summary:
Eric of Brandenburg (Erich von Brandenburg), born around 1245 and dying on December 28, 1295, was a scion of the powerful House of Ascania, specifically the Margraves of Brandenburg, whose brief and contested election as Archbishop of Magdeburg in 1295 underscored the complex interplay between secular dynastic ambition and ecclesiastical authority within the Holy Roman Empire. His tenure, lasting mere months and ending before his formal consecration, nevertheless illuminated the fierce political and spiritual struggles for control over one of the Empire's most significant archdioceses during the late 13th century. His life, though cut short, serves as a microcosm of the intense regional power dynamics that defined the post-Hohenstaufen era in Central Europe.

Eric's path to the archbishopric was paved by his noble birth as a son of Otto III, Margrave of Brandenburg, granting him immediate access to influential networks. Upon the death of Archbishop Burchard II of Querfurt in 1295, Eric was elected by the cathedral chapter of Magdeburg. This election, however, was immediately challenged by Burchard III of Querfurt, a relative of the deceased archbishop, who also claimed the see. This dispute was not merely theological but a naked power struggle between the Brandenburg Ascanian interests and the established Querfurt dynasty, reflecting broader tensions among princely houses vying for control over rich ecclesiastical territories. Eric’s unexpected death later that year, before Rome could confirm his election or the dispute could be fully resolved, abruptly ended this particular chapter of contention.
